title: Prove the sharp R-unit Gaussian bulk denominator (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. For the degree-R central Gaussian bulk `B=g(W)` from David Ganz's #5813, the constructive denominator debt is sharp:

```diff
- pi^R B is Gaussian-integral
+ min{d>=0: pi^d B is Gaussian-integral} = R
+ c_S = i^a/pi^R for every displacement |S|=R
```

The proof covers every n>=1, 0<=R<=n and 0<=a<=n-R. It also proves uniqueness among permutation-symmetric convolutions of Boolean degree at most R with that central-band response. Actual reachable input pairs show that obtaining the full response modulo pi^p generally requires numerator precision p+R; one fewer digit fails at every chosen output coordinate. A different formula in the stated radius class cannot reduce this debt.

The new result is the matching lower bound, uniqueness and precision witnesses. Ganz's interpolation and constructive upper bound remain credited. No predecessor verifier or numerical result was audited or replayed as the deliverable. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

## Evidence

- Before: #5813 supplies the R-unit numerator construction. Its denominator-accounting question leaves the sharpness issue open in this narrowed response class.
- After: README.md proves the lower bound from the literal top Boolean coefficient and supplies explicit indistinguishable-input witnesses. Walsh inversion and independent falling-factorial group-ring evaluation agree on the stated finite domain.
- Local CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass with identical source-hash-bound receipts: 285 bands, 114686 coefficients, 11263 top coefficients, 1022 independent polynomial coefficients, 350 literal Walsh eigenvalues, 75768 precision witnesses and sixteen boundary/semantic controls.
- Direct checks take 4.859 seconds normal and 4.814 seconds optimized. Both registered commands pass, with the complete registered invocation taking 10.093 seconds. Each command is below its 120-second timeout.
- Metadata, committed-byte/source-history preflight and staged whitespace pass. The official five-file export passes integrity checking. An isolated optimized replay from a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH passes and preserves all six files, including its export manifest, byte-for-byte and mode-for-mode.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
PY=/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
"$PY" -W error -B research/gaussian-bulk-sharp-denominator/verify.py
"$PY" -W error -O -B research/gaussian-bulk-sharp-denominator/verify.py
"$PY" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-bulk-sharp-denominator
"$PY" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-bulk-sharp-denominator --check-source-history
```

The standard-library verifier writes no files and imports no predecessor package. The stdout receipt binds the five package files by SHA256. SOURCES.json pins the base catalogue and selected record for provenance; pending predecessor heads are citations, not runtime dependencies.

## Limitations

The universal result rests on the written proof. Finite corroboration fixes n<=10; independent group-ring evaluation fixes n<=5, literal spectra n<=4, and precision witnesses n<=8 with p<=4. Restricted observables or input lattices, nonsymmetric responses and higher-degree replacements are outside the uniqueness obstruction. Physical delivery, exceptional correction, restoration, storage, movement, native admission and the complete caller bill remain open. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No Lean, complete multiplier, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Open next questions

- Allow one additional Krawtchouk degree and solve a small exact integrality system to test whether a higher-degree central-band response can lower the denominator.
- Pin an actual provider observable and determine whether composing it with B removes the worst denominator coefficients. Any useful continuation still needs the full paid caller and correction bill.

## Related open work

- #5813, David Ganz, head af37059809ae41283142c6aeb217cc456852aff1 supplies central four-phase interpolation and the R-unit upper construction. This proves its exact minimal denominator in the stated class and the matching precision necessity.
- #5815, David Ganz, head f0fcda576df410dc15cd5b8183d4f74d284eba2b supplies exceptional correction and mixed-precision constructions; no implementation bill is changed here.
- #5825, Ali Romman, head baea91d8c0044a0036006bdd3b4d7bce3d6cf783 bounds work for a specified standalone Newton-W graph. This is a realization-independent denominator obstruction within the fixed full-response class, without recomputing its work totals.
- #5880, Nick Petalas, studies reversible clean storage of the raw Gaussian tensor. Its endpoint and capacity quantity differ, and it is not an input lemma or the target of this contribution.

Completion refresh inspected this account's eight other open PRs created since the [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19215628): #5886, #5887, #5888, #5889, #5891, #5892, #5893 and #5895. None computes this central Gaussian bulk's minimal denominator or numerator-precision threshold. No additional computations were run to compare their results, and no shared numerical disagreement is claimed.

The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19215628) states this scope. Canonical main and priority revision 8 were refreshed before submission; main remains de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a. Live PRs, recent handoffs, reservations, all-main README searches and merged-result searches found no delivered denominator-sharpness result in the inspected coverage. Unpublished work and arbitrary code diffs remain outside that coverage.
